correctness.rationale: The q-binomial Newton identity expresses t^rank X as a finite linear combination of indicators of subgroups {X:XU=0}, with coefficients t^(n-j) product_{i<j}(1-q^i t). Character orthogonality yields Fourier eigenvalues lambda_s=sum_{j>=s} [n-s choose j-s]_q q^(m(n-j)) t^(n-j) product_{i<j}(1-q^i t). For 0<=t<q^-(n-1) each eigenvalue is strictly positive, and at q^-k precisely ranks s<=k have positive eigenvalues, giving the exact Gram rank. Outside those points the two top ranks have opposite signs: lambda_n=P(1-q^(n-1)t), lambda_(n-1)=P(1+(q^m-q^(n-1))t). Cases t=0,1, n=2 are included. Independent exact rank-2x2 Fourier characters over F2/F3 and support-boundary examples corroborate the identity; proof is for all fields and m>=n.
